title: server: implement validate_vorp
description: Implement server function to validate VORP (Value of Replacement Position) calculations for task prioritization. This ensures that priority scores accurately reflect the relative value of implementing features.

ubiquitous: THE SYSTEM SHALL calculate VORP scores for all prioritized tasks
THE SYSTEM SHALL normalize VORP scores across comparable task sets

event_driven.trigger: WHEN a task priority is set or updated
event_driven.shall: THE SYSTEM SHALL recalculate the VORP score based on current context
THE SYSTEM SHALL propagate VORP recalculation to affected tasks

unwanted.condition: IF VORP calculation would produce a negative value
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT assign the calculated value
unwanted.because: negative VORP values have no meaningful interpretation

unwanted.condition: IF required metrics for VORP are unavailable
unwanted.shall_not: THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT estimate placeholder values
unwanted.because: estimated values would compromise prioritization accuracy

preconditions: Task must have defined effort estimate
Task must have defined impact estimate
Baseline replacement value must be configured
postconditions: VORP score is a non-negative decimal value
VORP score is persisted with the task record
VORP calculation metadata is logged for audit
invariants: VORP calculation shall be reproducible for identical inputs
VORP scores shall remain comparable within the same project scope
Precision shall be maintained to at least 4 decimal places

happy: Given a task with high impact and low effort, when validate_vorp is called, then VORP score reflects high value relative to baseline
Given a task with standard metrics, when validate_vorp is called, then the score is calculated and stored correctly
Given multiple tasks, when validate_vorp is called for each, then relative ordering matches expected priority
error: Given a task with zero effort, when validate_vorp is called, then validation returns DIVISION_BY_ZERO error
Given a task with missing impact metrics, when validate_vorp is called, then validation returns MISSING_METRICS error
Given an unconfigured baseline, when validate_vorp is called, then validation returns BASELINE_NOT_CONFIGURED error
